# Adversarial Audit Findings — Run 1

**Date:** 2026-04-30  
**Models used:** gpt-4.1, gpt-5.2, gpt-5.3-codex, claude-sonnet-4, claude-opus-4.6  
**Scope:** All changes in working tree (`git diff HEAD`) — 577 additions across 14 files  
**Methodology:** adversarial-audit skill, single prompt to 5 models, triage below.

---

## Deduplicated Findings

### F1: `to_file_name` unconditionally strips leading `_` — breaks backward compat (FIXED)

**Found by:** 5/5 models  
**Severity:** HIGH  
**Status:** ✅ Fixed

The `to_file_name()` function stripped leading `_` from all filenames regardless of
`virtual_directories` config. This silently changes keys for any user with `_`-prefixed
files and can cause key collisions (`_foo.md` and `foo.md` → both become `foo`).

**Fix applied:** `to_file_name` now takes a `strip_underscore: bool` parameter, only
stripping when `virtual_directories=true`.

---

### F2: Envelope merge can produce duplicate `title` YAML key (FIXED)

**Found by:** 4/5 models (gpt-5.2, gpt-5.3-codex, claude-sonnet-4, claude-opus-4.6)  
**Severity:** HIGH  
**Status:** ✅ Fixed

When `frontmatter_document_title` is not set (or set to something other than `"title"`),
a frontmatter `title:` field would be merged into `extra`, creating a duplicate `title`
key in the YAML envelope alongside the built-in `document.title`.

**Fix applied:** Always skip `"title"` in the reserved-key filter (along with `"key"`,
`"parents"`, `"back-links"`), regardless of `frontmatter_document_title` config.

---

### F3: Bare frontmatter round-trip breaks when first key is not `title:`

**Found by:** 3/5 models (gpt-5.2, gpt-5.3-codex, claude-opus-4.6)  
**Severity:** HIGH  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged — design limitation

`wrap_bare_frontmatter()` only triggers when content starts with `title: `. If
`bare_frontmatter=true` and a file's frontmatter starts with `status: ready\ntitle: X`,
the write produces bare YAML starting with `status:`, which on re-read is NOT recognized
as frontmatter (metadata lost).

**Mitigation:** This is a known constraint of the bare frontmatter design — the spec
explicitly requires `title: ` as the first line for detection. The `frontmatter_document_title`
config determines which field is the title, and the writer should emit it first. This is
a pre-existing design decision from Phase 1, not introduced by the envelope change.

---

### F4: Virtual directory stale index files not cleaned up

**Found by:** 4/5 models  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged — known limitation

When all `.md` files are removed from a directory, the previously generated `_dirname.md`
lingers. No garbage collection of stale generated indices.

---

### F5: LSP server hardcodes `virtual_directories: false`

**Found by:** 3/5 models (gpt-5.2, gpt-5.3-codex, claude-opus-4.6)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged — intentional for safety

The LSP server (`iwes`) does not enable virtual directories to avoid file-system side
effects during editor sessions. This is conservative but creates inconsistency with CLI.

---

### F6: Virtual directory index generation has silent FS failures

**Found by:** 3/5 models  
**Severity:** LOW  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged

`fs::write` and `fs::remove_file` errors are silently ignored in `generate_virtual_indices`.
On read-only filesystems, indices won't be created with no error surfaced.

---

### F7: `--meta` filter parses YAML per document (performance)

**Found by:** 2/5 models  
**Severity:** LOW  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged — acceptable for current scale

---

### F8: Bare frontmatter can misclassify prose starting with `title: `

**Found by:** 2/5 models (gpt-5.2, claude-opus-4.6)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged — requires opt-in

Only applies when user explicitly enables `bare_frontmatter=true`. The detection
heuristic is intentionally simple; users opting in accept this constraint.

---

### F9: Non-mapping frontmatter (e.g. YAML sequence) is dropped silently

**Found by:** 1/5 models (gpt-5.3-codex)  
**Severity:** MEDIUM  
**Status:** ⚠️ Acknowledged

If frontmatter parses as a YAML sequence rather than mapping, the envelope merge
silently produces no extra fields, and `blocks_to_markdown_sparce_skip_frontmatter`
strips it from the body. Unlikely in practice.

---

## Q1 — Biggest Missed Opportunity

### gpt-4.1
> Native support for incremental, bidirectional, and real-time graph updates via an
> API or event stream. A persistent service exposing a live, queryable, updatable
> knowledge graph would enable agents to react to changes and coordinate in real time.

### gpt-5.2
> A first-class query + patch protocol: store parsed frontmatter as structured,
> indexed properties and expose a query language plus a transactional "apply patch"
> API with preconditions/ETags. Agents could plan → query → batch-edit → verify
> without brittle YAML string parsing.

### gpt-5.3-codex
> A transactional graph API for agents (structured query + patch operations with
> stable IDs, optimistic concurrency, and change streams) for safe multi-agent
> coordination without markdown text surgery.

### claude-sonnet-4
> Semantic change tracking and diff-aware context injection — temporal context
> (what changed, what's stale, dependency cascades) would shift iwe from static
> knowledge store to dynamic change-aware system.

### claude-opus-4.6
> A per-document patch/commit model (CRDTs or operational transforms) that allows
> agents to submit changes without locking the entire graph. Combined with change
> notifications, this enables concurrent multi-agent work.

### Synthesis
All 5 models converge on the same gap: **iwe lacks a transactional, incremental,
concurrent-safe mutation API**. The current batch model (load entire graph → mutate
→ write back) is the fundamental bottleneck for agent-driven workflows. The highest-impact
addition would be a structured query/patch protocol with change detection, enabling
multiple agents to work on different parts of the knowledge graph simultaneously without
full-graph serialization.

---

## Q2 — PR Acceptance Risk

### gpt-4.1
> File system side effects and data loss from virtual directory generation. Automatic
> file creation/deletion during read operations, plus lack of resource limits on YAML
> parsing. If safeguarded, reasonable for upstream.

### gpt-5.2
> Feature coherence + side effects: virtual directories materialize files and change
> key semantics in ways hard to make backward-compatible, dirtying working trees on
> read operations. As one PR, poor candidate — split and make strongly opt-in.

### gpt-5.3-codex
> Mixed-scope feature bundle with side-effectful reads. Split into focused PRs
> (meta filtering, bare frontmatter, retrieve envelope, virtual dirs separately)
> and make virtual-dir side effects explicitly opt-in.

### claude-sonnet-4
> Breaking API change in retrieve output format. The five features are loosely coupled;
> upstream maintainers prefer focused PRs. Missing documentation. With rework, acceptable.

### claude-opus-4.6
> The `to_file_name` `_` stripping was unconditional and broke backward compatibility
> (now fixed). Virtual directories writing files during load violates least surprise.
> Split into 3-4 focused PRs and gate virtual-dir side effects strictly.

### Synthesis
**Poor candidate as a single PR; good candidate when split.** The primary risks are:

1. **Side-effectful reads** — virtual directories writing files during `new_for_path_with_options`
   violates the expectation that loading is read-only.
2. **Feature bundling** — 5 distinct features in one PR increases review burden and
   complicates rollback.
3. **Retrieve output format change** — breaks existing consumers of the envelope.

Recommendation: split into 4 PRs (config plumbing + bare frontmatter, --meta filtering,
virtual directories, merged envelope), each with its own tests and documentation.
The `_`-stripping fix (F1) was the most damning blocker and is now resolved.

All tests pass. Let me summarize what I found and what was done.

## Diagnosis

I spent a long time investigating `wrap_bare_frontmatter()` in `crates/liwe/src/markdown.rs`, suspecting it was stripping YAML continuation lines (indented `- foo` items). The original code had a `cleaned_header` filter that removed lines starting with spaces — which would destroy YAML sequences. However, that code was **already removed** in the current HEAD.

The actual parsing pipeline works correctly for bare frontmatter: `wrap_bare_frontmatter()` wraps the header in `---` fences, pulldown-cmark parses it as a MetadataBlock, and `serde_yaml` correctly handles sequences. I confirmed this with extensive diagnostic tests.

The **actual bug** I found is in `crates/iwec/src/lib.rs` line 1370:

```rust
// from_documents_with_config() — used by MCP server tests
let graph = Graph::from_state(state, true, MarkdownOptions::default(), None);
//                                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
//                                         Ignores config.markdown!
```

`from_documents_with_config()` accepts a `Configuration` (which may have `bare_frontmatter: true`) but hardcodes `MarkdownOptions::default()` (where `bare_frontmatter: false`). This means **any MCP client using `iwe_find` with `--meta` on bare frontmatter documents would fail** — the bare frontmatter is never recognized, so no metadata is stored, so `--meta depends=foo` returns nothing.

## Fix Applied

**`crates/iwec/src/lib.rs` line 1370**: Changed `MarkdownOptions::default()` → `config.markdown.clone()` so that `from_documents_with_config` respects the configuration's markdown options including `bare_frontmatter`.

## Test Added

**`crates/liwe/tests/find_metadata_test.rs`**: Added `bare_frontmatter_meta_filter_finds_sequence_value` — tests that `--meta depends=foo` works with bare frontmatter documents containing YAML sequences.

All 80 test suites pass, 0 failures.
